scenes.line1: How do teams manage code changes?
scenes.say: Ever wonder how teams keep their code organized? Which branching strategy is right for your project?

scenes.label: Trunk
scenes.sub: One main branch, short feature branches merged often.
scenes.say: Trunk-based development uses a single main branch. Teams work on short-lived feature branches and merge changes back in quickly.

scenes.label: GitFlow
scenes.sub: Multiple branches for features, releases, and fixes.
scenes.say: GitFlow adds more structure. You get separate branches for features, releases, and hotfixes, which helps manage complex release cycles.
Feature flags let you merge unfinished work safely. You can turn features on or off at runtime without breaking the main branch.
Trunk-based is great for speed and simplicity. GitFlow is better when you need more control over releases and hotfixes.

scenes.question: Is GitFlow always the best choice?
scenes.wrong: Yes, more branches are always better.
scenes.right: Not always. Trunk-based can be faster for small, agile teams.
scenes.say: Be careful—more branches aren't always better. Sometimes, a simpler strategy like trunk-based is exactly what you need.
